anki-apkg fixture - provenance

What this is
  review.apkg is a genuine Anki 2.1 package: a ZIP holding collection.anki2 (a SQLite
  database with the col, notes and cards tables), a media map, and the media member it names.
  It contains one Basic note with two fields and one card that has been reviewed.

How it was made
  python build_fixture.py review.apkg
  The script is committed beside the fixture so the artifact can be rebuilt and compared, in the
  same way the obsidian fixture records how it was made. It writes Anki's own schema rather than a
  convenient approximation of it: fields are joined with the unit separator, the note type and
  deck are recorded as the JSON blobs Anki stores, and the card carries real scheduling numbers.

What it does NOT establish
  1. It was not produced or opened by the Anki application itself. Nothing here shows that Anki
     opens a package this project writes; that is a separate, human-facing check.
  2. It is not a workspace readback. No import path consumes .apkg yet, so no round-trip is
     claimed - only that the fixture is a real package for such a round-trip to be written against.
  3. It is one deck, one note type and one card. It says nothing about the range of Anki note
     types, options groups, filtered decks or review history a real collection can contain.
  4. It carries no human review. The scheduling numbers are written here, not earned by anyone
     answering a card, and must never be read as a person's study history.
